newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says ERM may wait until budget fully passed.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says ERM may wait until budget fully passed.

text.p: The Italian government may wait until the budget has been approved by both houses of parliament before seeking to push the lira back into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a newspaper interview.

The 1997 budget is due to be ratified by the lower house of parliament later on Saturday. The package will then pass to the upper house (Senate) which has until the end of the year to vote on the financial draft law.

Ciampi has previously said he would wait for ratification in the lower hosue before asking for the lira to return to the ERM, but in an interview with La Stampa daily he indicated that more time might be needed.
"The lower house still has to give the green light to the budget. We will then have to evaluate if this is enough or if we will have to wait for ratification in both houses," he said.
"We haven't yet established when or at what level the re-entry will take place...now it's a question of entering the home straight and deciding the most opportune moment," he added.
Most analysts expect the lira to return to the ERM in time for the European Union's Dublin summit on December 13-14. The lira crashed out of the currency grid in September 1992. REUTER
